prompt: Fact: "Octopuses have three hearts." — two ways of taking that in:

options.label: Read it and move on
options.content: The fact registers, feels reasonable, and you continue to the next sentence. It's now stored as roughly one isolated point in memory - accurate, but with no built connections leading back to it, and no reason it would be easier to recall later than any other single sentence you skimmed.

options.label: Ask and answer "why is that true?"
options.content: You work out (or look up) that two hearts pump blood to the gills, and a third pumps it to the rest of the body - and that this connects to octopuses using blue, copper-based blood instead of iron-based blood, which carries oxygen less efficiently and needs the extra pumping help. That's now three or four connection points instead of one isolated sentence - each one a separate path memory could later use to find its way back to the original fact.
